at åbne.explanation: "At åbne" means "to open". To ask a shop when it opens, say: "Hvornår åbner I?" (When do you open?)

sentence.da: Jeg vil **åbne** døren for dig.
sentence.en: I want to open the door for you.

at åbne op.explanation: "At åbne op" means "to open up". When you mean to make something possible, use "åbne op for": "Det åbner op for nye muligheder" (It opens up new possibilities).

sentence.da: Kan du **åbne op**? Jeg står udenfor.
sentence.en: Can you open up? I am standing outside.

at ånde.explanation: "At ånde" means "to breathe". To say you cannot breathe, use "trække vejret" (literally, to pull the breath): "Jeg kan ikke trække vejret" (I cannot breathe).

sentence.da: Det er svært at **ånde** i så tyk røg.
sentence.en: It is hard to breathe in such thick smoke.

en å.explanation: "En å" means "a stream", as in flowing water. To talk about a stream: "Der er fisk i åen" (There are fish in the stream). Do not mix it up with "en flod" (a river). To talk about a big river: "Floden er meget bred" (The river is very wide).

sentence.da: Vi gik en tur langs den smalle **å**.
sentence.en: We took a walk along the narrow stream.

en åbning.explanation: "En åbning" means "an opening". When you talk about the start of an event, it also means "an opening": "Åbningen af udstillingen er i morgen" (The opening of the exhibition is tomorrow).

sentence.da: Katten fandt en lille **åbning** i hegnet.
sentence.en: The cat found a small opening in the fence.

en åbningsdag.explanation: "En åbningsdag" means "an opening day". It is built from "åbning" (opening) and "dag" (day).

sentence.da: Der var lang kø foran butikken på dens **åbningsdag**.
sentence.en: There was a long line in front of the shop on its opening day.

en åbningstid.explanation: "En åbningstid" means "an opening hour". To ask when a shop is open, use the plural "åbningstider": "Hvad er butikkens åbningstider?" (What are the shop's opening hours?)

sentence.da: Butikkens **åbningstid** er fra ni til fem.
sentence.en: The shop's opening hours are from nine to five.

en åkande.explanation: "En åkande" means "a water lily". To name its leaf, add "blad" (leaf): "et åkandeblad" (a water lily leaf).

sentence.da: En **åkande** har runde blade, der flyder på vandet.
sentence.en: A water lily has round leaves that float on the water.

en ål.explanation: "En ål" means "an eel". Do not mix it up with "en å" (a stream). To talk about an eel: "Vi fangede en ål" (We caught an eel). To talk about a stream: "Åen er smal" (The stream is narrow).

sentence.da: En **ål** lever i vand og ligner en slange.
sentence.en: An eel lives in water and looks like a snake.

en ånd.explanation: "En ånd" means "a spirit", as in a being without a body. When you talk about the main idea behind something, it means "the spirit": "lovens ånd" (the spirit of the law).

sentence.da: Børnene tror, at der bor en **ånd** i det gamle hus.
sentence.en: The children believe that a spirit lives in the old house.

en årring.explanation: "En årring" means "a tree ring". It is built from "et år" (a year) and "en ring" (a ring), because each ring is one year of growth. To say how to find the age of a tree, use "tælle" (to count): "Man tæller årringene for at finde træets alder" (You count the tree rings to find the age of the tree).

sentence.da: Hver **årring** i stammen viser et år i træets liv.
sentence.en: Each tree ring in the trunk shows one year in the tree's life.

en årsag.explanation: "En årsag" means "a reason", as in the cause of something. To name a cause, say: "Årsagen til branden er ukendt" (The reason for the fire is unknown). Do not mix it up with "en grund" (a reason). To give a reason for doing something, use "grund": "Jeg har en god grund til at blive hjemme" (I have a good reason to stay home).

sentence.da: Der må være en **årsag** til, at bilen ikke starter.
sentence.en: There must be a reason why the car does not start.

en årsopgørelse.explanation: "En årsopgørelse" means "an annual tax statement". It is built from "år" (year) and "opgørelse" (statement). A fact about Denmark: the Danish tax authorities send one to every taxpayer.

sentence.da: Jeg kan se på min **årsopgørelse**, at jeg får penge tilbage.
sentence.en: I can see on my annual statement that I get money back.

en årstid.explanation: "En årstid" means "a season". To name your favorite, say: "Efteråret er min yndlingsårstid" (Autumn is my favorite season). Do not mix it up with "en sæson" (a season of a show or sport). For example, "Sæsonen starter i dag" (The season starts today).

sentence.da: Vinter er en kold **årstid**, og sommer er en varm.
sentence.en: Winter is a cold season, and summer is a warm one.

et åbent hus.explanation: "Et åbent hus" means "an open house". When a house is for sale and buyers may visit, it also means "an open house": "Der er åbent hus søndag klokken to" (There is an open house on Sunday at two o'clock).

sentence.da: Skolen holder **åbent hus** på lørdag.
sentence.en: The school has an open house on Saturday.

et år.explanation: "Et år" means "a year". To say your age, add "gammel" (old): "Jeg er tredive år gammel" (I am thirty years old).

sentence.da: Der er tolv måneder i et **år**.
sentence.en: There are twelve months in a year.

et århundrede.explanation: "Et århundrede" means "a century". It is built from "år" (year) and "hundrede" (hundred). To name a period, use a number with a dot: "i det 21. århundrede" (in the 21st century).

sentence.da: Huset er næsten et **århundrede** gammelt.
sentence.en: The house is almost a century old.

et årstal.explanation: "Et årstal" means "a year (date)". To say that a number is a year: "1990 er et årstal" (1990 is a year). Do not mix it up with "et år" (a year as a length of time). To say how long: "tre år" (three years).

sentence.da: Hvilket **årstal** blev huset bygget?
sentence.en: Which year was the house built?

et årti.explanation: "Et årti" means "a decade". To name a decade, add "-erne" to the number: "firserne" (the eighties).

sentence.da: Vi har boet her i mere end et **årti**.
sentence.en: We have lived here for more than a decade.

åben.explanation: "Åben" means "open". To talk about the action, use the verb "at åbne" (to open): "Jeg åbner døren" (I open the door).

sentence.da: Butikken er **åben** til klokken seks.
sentence.en: The shop is open until six o'clock.

åbenbart.explanation: "Åbenbart" means "apparently". It comes from the word "åbenbar" (obvious). To say you have just noticed something, say: "Du har åbenbart ikke hørt det" (You have apparently not heard it).

sentence.da: Han er **åbenbart** syg i dag.
sentence.en: He is apparently sick today.

åbenlys.explanation: "Åbenlys" means "obvious". It is built from "åben" (open) and "lys" (light). To say something is clearly true, say: "Det er åbenlyst, at hun har ret" (It is obvious that she is right).

sentence.da: Hans løgn var **åbenlys**, og alle kunne se det.
sentence.en: His lie was obvious, and everyone could see it.

åbningstider.explanation: "Åbningstider" means "opening hours". It is built from "åbning" (opening) and "tider" (times).

sentence.da: Butikkens **åbningstider** er fra ni til seks.
sentence.en: The shop's opening hours are from nine to six.

åndelig.explanation: "Åndelig" means "spiritual". It comes from "en ånd" (a spirit). To say someone looks for spiritual help, say: "Han søger åndelig vejledning" (He seeks spiritual guidance). Do not mix it up with "psykisk" (mental). To talk about the mind, say: "Hun har psykiske problemer" (She has mental problems).

sentence.da: Hun søger ro og **åndelig** styrke i naturen.
sentence.en: She seeks peace and spiritual strength in nature.

årlig.explanation: "Årlig" means "annual". To say how often something happens, use "årligt" (annually): "Det sker årligt" (It happens every year).

sentence.da: Vi har en **årlig** fest i juni.
sentence.en: We have an annual party in June.

årvågen.explanation: "Årvågen" means "alert". The last part, "vågen" (awake), also stands alone. For example, "Jeg er vågen" (I am awake).

sentence.da: Natvagten må være **årvågen** og lægge mærke til alt.
sentence.en: The night guard must be alert and notice everything.
